answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a scarce, time-locked resource — like a verifiable work history or a bond that unlocks slowly — before it can transact. Like a falcon that must prove its hunt before joining the flock, an agent earns trust only through accumulated, costly, checkable actions. A walnut's hard shell is a good analogy: the cost of cracking it deters cheap copies, while a lantern of public attestations lights up which identities have a real, auditable past. Cheap clones cannot fake that history.
